newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean ruling party chief meets union leaders.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean ruling party chief meets union leaders.

text.p: The chairman of South Korea's ruling party made a dramatic visit to a Seoul cathedral on Monday to meet militant union leaders in a last minute bid to head off the biggest strike in the country's history.
Witnesses said Lee Hong-koo was escorted to a building on the Myongdong Cathedral grounds by about 30 chanting workers to meet heads of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions.
"Get out, Get out," workers screamed as Lee was ushered past a ramshackle tent used by confederation leaders as their strike headquarters for almost three weeks.
The confederation has threatened to bring out its 500,000 members on Wednesday, joining an all-out stoppage by the 1.2 million-strong Federation of Korean Trade Unions scheduled to begin on Tuesday.
On Saturday Lee challenged union leaders to a televised debate over a new labour law that has sparked strikes idling the auto industry and disrupting other key sectors of the export-led economy.
But confederation leader Kwon Young-kil dismissed the offer as a propaganda ploy.
